# Xu Zhang

> Publication index of Xu Zhang (School of Computing, Macquarie University). Topics: speech emotion recognition, emotional text-to-speech for diffusion and flow-matching models, urban flow and origin-destination demand prediction, hyperspectral image classification. ORCID 0000-0002-4143-0715. GitHub @CodeZx6.

Preferred citation format for any paper: use the BibTeX at https://codezx6.github.io/publications.bib. Each paper page below contains a TL;DR, key points, abstract, DOI or arXiv ID, and BibTeX.

## Publications

- [DUET: Unified Dual-Space Emotion Control for Diffusion and Flow-Matching Driven Text-to-Speech](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/duet.html): Xu Zhang, Longbing Cao, Zhangkai Wu. arXiv:2606.00066 (2026). arXiv:2606.00066. DUET adds fine-grained, plug-and-play emotion control to pretrained diffusion and flow-matching TTS models by steering a linearly decodable emotion direction in hidden space and guiding the mel output through a differentiable vocoder, with no retraining. Also known as: DUET TTS; dual-space emotion control; training-free emotional text-to-speech; emotion control for pretrained diffusion TTS; emotion control for flow-matching TTS.
- [PhysioSER: Learning Physiology-Informed Vocal Spectrotemporal Representations for Speech Emotion Recognition](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/physioser.html): Xu Zhang, Longbing Cao, Runze Yang, Zhangkai Wu. arXiv:2602.13259 (2026). arXiv:2602.13259. PhysioSER couples vocal amplitude and phase through voice anatomy and physiology (VAP) informed quaternion representations, aligned with a frozen self-supervised backbone, giving an interpretable and efficient plug-and-play speech emotion recognizer validated on 14 datasets and 10 languages. Also known as: PhysioSER; physiology-informed speech emotion recognition; voice anatomy and physiology (VAP) features; amplitude and phase views for SER; quaternion convolution for speech emotion.
- [DSTCN: Exploiting dynamic spatio-temporal correlations for origin-destination demand prediction](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/dstcn.html): Yongshun Gong, Piao Yu, Xu Zhang, Xinxin Zhang, Xiushan Nie, Haoliang Sun. Expert Systems with Applications, vol. 299, 130095 (2026). DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2025.130095. DSTCN (Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Correlation Network) forecasts origin-destination demand with three modules: Glstm2D for bidirectional origin/destination demand trends, Simformer for Transformer-based inter-regional similarity over the OD matrix, and FF-TM for temporal fusion; it beats state-of-the-art baselines on NYC-TOD2018, NYC-TOD2019, and HZMetro. Also known as: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Correlation Network; DSTCN OD demand; origin-destination demand forecasting; OD matrix prediction; metro OD demand prediction.
- [S2CMEN: A Mutually Enhancement Network for Superpixel Segmentation and Classification of Hyperspectral Image](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mutual-enhancement-hsi.html): Mengxin Cao, Yongmin Li, Xu Zhang, Guixin Zhao, Guohua Lv, Aimei Dong, Jinyong Cheng, Wei Li, Xiangjun Dong. IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 63, 1–14 (2025). DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2025.3608942. A network in which superpixel segmentation and hyperspectral classification reinforce each other, so segmentation boundaries and class predictions improve jointly. Also known as: S2CMEN; Superpixel Segmentation and Classification Mutual Enhancement Network; GSAM global spatial adaptive module; ASSN adaptive spectral-superpixel network; SSFM spatial-spectral fusion module.
- [MR-UFP: Enhancing urban flow prediction via mutual reinforcement with multi-scale regional information](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mr-ufp.html): Xu Zhang, Mengxin Cao, Yongshun Gong, Xiaoming Wu, Xiangjun Dong, Ying Guo, Long Zhao, Chengqi Zhang. Neural Networks, vol. 182, 106900 (2025). DOI 10.1016/j.neunet.2024.106900. MR-UFP improves urban flow prediction on small or noisy data by pre-training with spatial-temporal masking and contrastive learning, then jointly training the predictor with a multi-scale region-classification task that mutually reinforces spatial features. Also known as: MR-UFP; mutual reinforcement urban flow prediction; multi-scale regional information; spatial-temporal random masking pre-training; spatial-temporal contrastive pre-training.
- [BiST-IF: Enhancing origin–destination flow prediction via bi-directional spatio-temporal inference and interconnected feature evolution](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/bist-if.html): Piao Yu, Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Jian Zhang, Haoliang Sun, Junjie Zhang, Xinxin Zhang, Yilong Yin. Expert Systems with Applications, vol. 264, 125679 (2025). DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2024.125679. BiST-IF predicts metro and taxi origin-destination flows by correcting delayed OD matrices, applying bi-directional origin/destination attention, and letting OD and arrival (Out-OD) flows evolve jointly through mutual-information attention. Also known as: BiST-IF; OD flow prediction with delay correction; Out-OD flow; arrival OD flow; OD delay correction ODDC.
- [Enhanced-attention leaf disease recognition: Automatic visual recognition for leaf disease based on enhanced attention mechanism](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/leaf-disease-attention.html): Yumeng Yao, Xiaodun Deng, Xu Zhang, Junming Li, Wenxuan Sun, Gechao Zhang. PeerJ Computer Science, vol. 10, e2365 (2024). DOI 10.7717/peerj-cs.2365. An enhanced-attention vision model for fast and accurate recognition of tomato leaf diseases, aimed at early disease prevention in agriculture. Also known as: tomato leaf disease recognition; plant leaf disease detection; multi-head attention for small lesion detection; Focaler-SIoU loss; leaf disease detection in complex backgrounds.
- [S3CFSL: Spatial-Spectral–Semantic Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning for Hyperspectral Image Classification](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/spatial-spectral-semantic-fsl.html): Mengxin Cao, Xu Zhang, Jinyong Cheng, Guixin Zhao, Wei Li, Xiangjun Dong. IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 62, 1–15 (2024). DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2024.3434484. A cross-domain few-shot learner for hyperspectral images that jointly exploits spatial, spectral, and semantic information to classify new scenes from very few labelled samples. Also known as: S3CFSL; spatial-spectral-semantic cross-domain few-shot learning; cross-domain few-shot hyperspectral classification; SSDC spatial and spectral dual channels; CSST cross-spatial-spectral transformer.
- [ST-CSL: Spatio-temporal fusion and contrastive learning for urban flow prediction](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/st-csl.html): Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Chengqi Zhang, Xiaoming Wu, Ying Guo, Wenpeng Lu, Long Zhao, Xiangjun Dong. Knowledge-Based Systems, vol. 282, 111104 (2023). DOI 10.1016/j.knosys.2023.111104. ST-CSL fuses temporal-view and spatial-view contrastive learning so an urban flow predictor captures global periodicity and the hidden flow relationships between functionally similar regions. Also known as: ST-CSL; spatio-temporal fusion and contrastive learning; temporal-view contrastive learning; spatial-view contrastive learning; urban flow periodicity.
- [MCSTL: Mask- and Contrast-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Learning for Urban Flow Prediction](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mcstl.html): Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Xinxin Zhang, Xiaoming Wu, Chengqi Zhang, Xiangjun Dong. CIKM 2023, pp. 3298–3307. DOI 10.1145/3583780.3614958. MCSTL pre-trains an urban flow model with a mask-reconstruction task across space and time and a graph-based contrastive task that weights regions by inter-regional attention, then fine-tunes for flow prediction. Also known as: MCSTL; mask- and contrast-enhanced spatio-temporal learning; masked pre-training for urban flow; contrastive pre-training for traffic flow; global-local cross-attention.
- [URMDet-SimFire: Trustworthy multimodal detection with uncertainty and reliability modeling for fire and smoke analytics](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/urmdet-simfire.html): Zhonghua Dang, Xu Zhang. Array, vol. 31, 101124 (2026). DOI 10.1016/j.array.2026.101124. A trustworthy multimodal fire-and-smoke detector that models uncertainty and reliability of each modality. Also known as: URMDet-SimFire; trustworthy fire and smoke detection; multimodal fire detection; uncertainty and reliability modeling for object detection; smoke analytics.

## DUET: Unified Dual-Space Emotion Control for Diffusion and Flow-Matching Driven Text-to-Speech

Authors: Xu Zhang, Longbing Cao, Zhangkai Wu
Venue: arXiv:2606.00066 (2026)
arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00066
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/duet.html
Keywords: emotional text-to-speech, emotion control, diffusion TTS, flow-matching TTS, activation steering, classifier guidance, plug-and-play, humanoid robot, Ameca
Also described as: DUET TTS; dual-space emotion control; training-free emotional text-to-speech; emotion control for pretrained diffusion TTS; emotion control for flow-matching TTS; hidden-space steering for speech synthesis; mel-space guidance with a differentiable vocoder; linearly decodable emotion direction in TTS hidden states; emotion and speaker identity disentanglement; plug-and-play emotional speech synthesis; controllable expressive TTS without fine-tuning; emotional speech for humanoid robots

TL;DR: DUET adds fine-grained, plug-and-play emotion control to pretrained diffusion and flow-matching TTS models by steering a linearly decodable emotion direction in hidden space and guiding the mel output through a differentiable vocoder, with no retraining.

Task: Emotion-controllable text-to-speech (emotional TTS)
Model type: Inference-time control for pretrained diffusion and flow-matching TTS; no backbone fine-tuning
Core finding: Emotion is a linearly decodable direction of frozen hidden states, nearly orthogonal to the speaker-identity direction
Mechanism: Hidden-space steering + mel-space guidance in one per-step update
Evaluation: 5 architecturally diverse pretrained TTS backbones, 3 datasets, 10 supervised emotional-TTS baselines, human rating of emotion appropriateness
Deployment: Ameca humanoid robot

Q: What problem does DUET solve?
A: Diffusion and flow-matching TTS models sound natural but have no explicit emotion control because emotional signals are entangled with speaker identity. DUET adds fine-grained emotion control to such pretrained models without retraining them.

Q: What is the key discovery behind DUET?
A: Emotion embedding emerges as a linearly decodable direction in the frozen hidden states of these models, and that direction is nearly orthogonal to the direction that encodes speaker identity. This makes emotion steerable without changing who is speaking.

Q: Does DUET require training or fine-tuning the TTS model?
A: No. DUET is plug-and-play: it intervenes during generation with a single per-step update that combines hidden-space steering along the target emotion direction and mel-space guidance through gradients from a differentiable vocoder.

Q: How was DUET evaluated?
A: On five architecturally diverse pretrained TTS backbones across three datasets, where it outperforms 10 supervised state-of-the-art emotional TTS baselines and achieves the highest human-rated emotion appropriateness. It was also deployed on an Ameca humanoid robot.

中文标题: DUET：面向扩散与流匹配文本转语音的统一双空间情感控制
中文摘要: 扩散式与流匹配式 TTS 自然度高但缺乏显式情感控制，因为情感信号与说话人身份纠缠。我们发现情感嵌入是冻结隐状态中一个线性可解码的方向，且几乎与说话人身份方向正交。据此提出即插即用框架 DUET：生成时在单次逐步更新中统一双空间控制，隐空间 steering 沿目标情感方向平移，Mel 空间 guidance 通过可微分声码器反传梯度细化频谱。在 5 个结构各异的预训练 TTS 骨干和 3 个数据集上，DUET 超过 10 个有监督情感 TTS 基线，并获得最高的人工情感恰当性评分；已部署于 Ameca 人形机器人。
中文关键词: 情感语音合成；情感可控 TTS；扩散模型语音合成；流匹配 TTS；隐空间引导；无需微调；即插即用；人形机器人；Ameca；张旭 麦考瑞大学

Key points:
- Emotion is a linearly decodable direction in the frozen hidden states of diffusion and flow-matching TTS models, and it is nearly orthogonal to the speaker-identity direction.
- DUET unifies hidden-space steering and mel-space guidance in a single per-step update during sampling, so any pretrained backbone gains emotion control without fine-tuning.
- Evaluated on five architecturally different pretrained TTS backbones and three datasets, DUET outperforms 10 supervised emotional-TTS baselines and receives the highest human-rated emotion appropriateness.
- Deployed on an Ameca humanoid robot to produce expressive emotional speech for embodied interaction.

Abstract: Diffusion and flow-matching based text-to-speech (TTS) models excel in naturalness but often lack explicit emotion control, as emotional signals remain entangled with speaker identity. We discover that emotion embedding emerges as a linearly decodable direction of frozen hidden states, nearly orthogonal to the direction embedding speaker identity. This inspires a plug-and-play framework DUET for emotion control over pretrained diffusion and flow-matching based TTS models. During generation, DUET unifies dual-space control to achieve fine-grained emotion intervention in a single per-step update: hidden space steering shifts generation along the target emotion direction, while mel-space guidance refines spectral details through gradients backpropagated from a differentiable vocoder. We validate DUET on five architecturally diverse pretrained TTS backbones across three datasets, where it outperforms 10 supervised state-of-the-art emotional TTS baselines across paradigms and achieves the highest human-rated emotion appropriateness. To further showcase its qualitative behavior, we deploy DUET on an Ameca humanoid robot, where it produces richly expressive emotional speech on the humanoid, demonstrating the strong potential for plug-and-play affective interaction for embodied agents.

## Learning Physiology-Informed Vocal Spectrotemporal Representations for Speech Emotion Recognition

Authors: Xu Zhang, Longbing Cao, Runze Yang, Zhangkai Wu
Venue: arXiv:2602.13259 (2026)
arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.13259
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/physioser.html
Keywords: speech emotion recognition, physiology-informed, quaternion convolution, amplitude and phase, self-supervised speech models, interpretable SER, humanoid robot
Also described as: PhysioSER; physiology-informed speech emotion recognition; voice anatomy and physiology (VAP) features; amplitude and phase views for SER; quaternion convolution for speech emotion; Hamilton-structured quaternion convolution; Contrastive Projection and Alignment (CPA); plug-in emotion head for frozen SSL speech models; interpretable and efficient SER; multilingual speech emotion recognition 10 languages; speech emotion recognition on humanoid robots; glottal source and vocal tract filter emotion cues

TL;DR: PhysioSER couples vocal amplitude and phase through voice anatomy and physiology (VAP) informed quaternion representations, aligned with a frozen self-supervised backbone, giving an interpretable and efficient plug-and-play speech emotion recognizer validated on 14 datasets and 10 languages.

Task: Speech emotion recognition (SER), utterance level
Model type: Compact plug-and-play module on top of a frozen self-supervised (SSL) speech backbone
Inputs: Physiology-informed amplitude and phase views (vocal-tract filter and glottal source)
Mechanism: Quaternion embedding + Hamilton-structured quaternion convolutions; Contrastive Projection and Alignment with the SSL branch; shallow attention fusion head
Evaluation: 14 datasets, 10 languages, 6 SSL backbones
Deployment: Real-time on a humanoid robotic platform

Q: What is PhysioSER?
A: A physiology-informed method for speech emotion recognition that builds amplitude and phase views of the voice from vocal anatomy and physiology, models their interaction with quaternion convolutions, and aligns them with a frozen self-supervised speech model.

Q: Why model phase as well as amplitude?
A: Physiological research shows that the dynamics of vocal amplitude and phase correlate with emotion through the vocal tract filter and the glottal source, yet most deep SER models use amplitude only and never couple the two.

Q: Can PhysioSER be added to an existing SSL model such as WavLM or HuBERT?
A: Yes. It is designed as a compact plug-and-play branch that complements a frozen SSL backbone; the two branches are aligned by Contrastive Projection and Alignment and fused by a shallow attention head.

Q: How broadly was it tested?
A: Across 14 datasets, 10 languages, and 6 backbones, with real-time deployment on a humanoid robot.

中文标题: 学习生理信息引导的嗓音时频表示用于语音情感识别（PhysioSER）
中文摘要: 语音情感识别对社交机器人与机器人心理评估等任务至关重要，但现有深度模型大多不可解释，且几乎只使用幅度信息。嗓音生理学表明，幅度与相位的动态通过声道滤波器和声门源与情感相关。PhysioSER 基于发声解剖与生理（VAP）构造幅度与相位视图，将其嵌入四元数域并用 Hamilton 结构四元数卷积建模二者交互；另一分支为冻结的自监督语音模型。两路话语级特征通过对比投影对齐框架对齐，再由浅层注意力融合头分类。在 14 个数据集、10 种语言、6 种骨干上验证了其可解释性与效率，并在人形机器人上实时部署。
中文关键词: 语音情感识别；发声生理学；幅度与相位；四元数卷积；自监督语音模型；可解释；即插即用；多语言情感识别；人形机器人；张旭 麦考瑞大学

Key points:
- Most deep SER models use amplitude only; PhysioSER builds amplitude and phase views grounded in vocal-tract and glottal-source physiology and models their interaction with Hamilton-structured quaternion convolutions.
- A Contrastive Projection and Alignment framework aligns the physiology branch with a frozen SSL backbone, followed by a shallow attention fusion head.
- Evaluated across 14 datasets, 10 languages, and 6 SSL backbones, and deployed in real time on a humanoid robotic platform.

Abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is essential for humanoid robot tasks such as social robotic interactions and robotic psychological diagnosis, where interpretable and efficient models are critical for safety and performance. Existing deep models trained on large datasets remain largely uninterpretable, often insufficiently modeling underlying emotional acoustic signals and failing to capture and analyze the core physiology of emotional vocal behaviors. Physiological research on human voices shows that the dynamics of vocal amplitude and phase correlate with emotions through the vocal tract filter and the glottal source. However, most existing deep models solely involve amplitude but fail to couple the physiological features of and between amplitude and phase. Here, we propose PhysioSER, a physiology-informed vocal spectrotemporal representation learning method, to address these issues with a compact, plug-and-play design. PhysioSER constructs amplitude and phase views informed by voice anatomy and physiology (VAP) to complement SSL models for SER. This VAP-informed framework incorporates two parallel workflows: a vocal feature representation branch to decompose vocal signals based on VAP, embed them into a quaternion field, and use Hamilton-structured quaternion convolutions for modeling their dynamic interactions; and a latent representation branch based on a frozen SSL backbone. Then, utterance-level features from both workflows are aligned by a Contrastive Projection and Alignment framework, followed by a shallow attention fusion head for SER classification. PhysioSER is shown to be interpretable and efficient for SER through extensive evaluations across 14 datasets, 10 languages, and 6 backbones, and its practical efficacy is validated by real-time deployment on a humanoid robotic platform.

## Exploiting dynamic spatio-temporal correlations for origin-destination demand prediction

Authors: Yongshun Gong, Piao Yu, Xu Zhang, Xinxin Zhang, Xiushan Nie, Haoliang Sun
Venue: Expert Systems with Applications, vol. 299, 130095 (2026)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2025.130095
Code: https://github.com/CodeZx6/DSTCN
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/dstcn.html
Keywords: origin-destination demand prediction, metro OD matrix, spatio-temporal correlation, graph convolution, attention, intelligent transportation
Also described as: Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Correlation Network; DSTCN OD demand; origin-destination demand forecasting; OD matrix prediction; metro OD demand prediction; taxi OD demand prediction New York; Glstm2D bidirectional demand trend modeling; Simformer Transformer spatial similarity module; FF-TM temporal fusion module; NYC-TOD2018; NYC-TOD2019; HZMetro

TL;DR: DSTCN (Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Correlation Network) forecasts origin-destination demand with three modules: Glstm2D for bidirectional origin/destination demand trends, Simformer for Transformer-based inter-regional similarity over the OD matrix, and FF-TM for temporal fusion; it beats state-of-the-art baselines on NYC-TOD2018, NYC-TOD2019, and HZMetro.

Task: Origin-destination (OD) demand prediction for intelligent transportation systems
Components: Glstm2D (bidirectional origin/destination demand trend), Simformer (Transformer-based inter-regional similarity over the OD matrix), FF-TM (temporal fusion and modelling)
Datasets: NYC-TOD2018, NYC-TOD2019, HZMetro
Open access: Yes, CC BY

Q: What does DSTCN predict?
A: Next-step origin-destination demand, i.e. how many trips will start in each region and end in each other region, which supports real-time traffic management, vehicle dispatch, and resource allocation.

Q: What are the three components of DSTCN?
A: Glstm2D jointly learns demand evolution from the origin and destination perspectives; Simformer uses a Transformer to extract dynamic inter-regional correlations across the OD matrix; FF-TM fuses multi-source spatio-temporal features for prediction.

Q: Which datasets were used?
A: Three large-scale real-world datasets: NYC-TOD2018, NYC-TOD2019 (New York taxi OD) and HZMetro (Hangzhou metro).

中文标题: 利用动态时空相关性进行起讫点（OD）需求预测
中文摘要: 准确的 OD 需求预测是智能交通系统的基础。OD 需求具有复杂、动态且高度耦合的时空模式。我们提出动态时空相关网络 DSTCN，包含三个模块：双向需求趋势建模模块 Glstm2D，从起点与终点两个视角联合学习需求演化；基于 Transformer 的空间相似性模块 Simformer，动态提取并整合 OD 矩阵上的区域间相关性；时间融合建模模块 FF-TM，融合多源时空特征完成下一步预测。在 NYC-TOD2018、NYC-TOD2019 和 HZMetro 三个大规模真实数据集上，DSTCN 稳定优于最新基线。
中文关键词: OD 需求预测；起讫点矩阵；动态时空相关；Transformer；地铁客流预测；出租车需求预测；智能交通；开放获取

Key points:
- Glstm2D jointly learns demand evolution from both the origin and the destination perspective.
- Simformer dynamically extracts and integrates inter-regional correlations across the OD matrix with a Transformer.
- FF-TM combines multi-source spatio-temporal features for next-step prediction.
- Evaluated on three large-scale real-world datasets (NYC-TOD2018, NYC-TOD2019, HZMetro); published open access (CC BY) in Expert Systems with Applications, vol. 299 (2026), online October 2025.

Abstract: Accurate Origin-Destination (OD) demand prediction is fundamental to intelligent transportation systems (ITS), enabling real-time traffic management, dynamic vehicle dispatch, and efficient resource allocation in urban environments. However, OD demand exhibits complex, dynamic, and highly coupled spatio-temporal patterns that remain challenging for existing models. We propose a novel Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Correlation Network (DSTCN) for OD demand forecasting. DSTCN features three key components: (1) a bidirectional demand trend modeling module (Glstm2D) that jointly learns demand evolution from both origin and destination perspectives; (2) a Transformer-based spatial similarity module (Simformer) to dynamically extract and integrate inter-regional correlations across the OD matrix; and (3) a temporal fusion and modeling module (FF-TM) that combines and processes multi-source spatio-temporal features for next-step prediction. Extensive experiments on three large-scale real-world datasets (NYC-TOD2018, NYC-TOD2019, and HZMetro) demonstrate that DSTCN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse urban scenarios.

## A Mutually Enhancement Network for Superpixel Segmentation and Classification of Hyperspectral Image

Authors: Mengxin Cao, Yongmin Li, Xu Zhang, Guixin Zhao, Guohua Lv, Aimei Dong, Jinyong Cheng, Wei Li, Xiangjun Dong
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 63, 1–14 (2025)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1109/TGRS.2025.3608942
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mutual-enhancement-hsi.html
Keywords: hyperspectral image classification, superpixel segmentation, mutual enhancement, remote sensing, deep learning
Also described as: S2CMEN; Superpixel Segmentation and Classification Mutual Enhancement Network; GSAM global spatial adaptive module; ASSN adaptive spectral-superpixel network; SSFM spatial-spectral fusion module; mutual enhancement strategy MES; graph convolutional network for hyperspectral classification; superpixel-based HSI classification; global spatial context hyperspectral; Indian Pines Pavia University Houston

TL;DR: A network in which superpixel segmentation and hyperspectral classification reinforce each other, so segmentation boundaries and class predictions improve jointly.

Task: Hyperspectral image (HSI) classification
Idea: Superpixel segmentation and classification enhance each other under a unit loss
Modules: GSAM (ASSN + GCN) for global spatial correlation; SSFM for spatial-spectral fusion; MES mutual enhancement strategy
Datasets and overall accuracy: Indian Pines 97.38%, Pavia University 92.33%, Houston 91.38%

Q: What is new in S2CMEN?
A: Most HSI classifiers use local patch-level spectral-spatial cues. S2CMEN adds global spatial contextual correlation by adaptively deriving superpixels from the image and letting the segmentation and classification losses reinforce each other.

Q: Can GSAM be reused with other models?
A: Yes. The global spatial adaptive module provides a transferable global spatial representation that can be integrated with other spectral feature extraction models.

Q: What accuracy does it reach?
A: Overall accuracies of 97.38% on Indian Pines, 92.33% on Pavia University, and 91.38% on Houston.

中文标题: 用于高光谱图像超像素分割与分类的互增强网络（S2CMEN）
中文摘要: 现有高光谱图像分类方法多依赖块级局部光谱-空间线索，较少利用像素间的全局空间上下文相关性。我们提出超像素分割与分类互增强网络 S2CMEN：全局空间自适应模块 GSAM 由自适应光谱-超像素网络 ASSN 与图卷积网络 GCN 组成，自适应地从高光谱图像中导出超像素并捕获全局空间关系，且可迁移到其他光谱特征提取模型；空间-光谱融合模块 SSFM 融合全局空间特征与光谱特征；在统一损失约束下，互增强策略 MES 使分割损失与分类损失相互促进。在 Indian Pines、Pavia University、Houston 上总体精度分别为 97.38%、92.33%、91.38%。
中文关键词: 高光谱图像分类；超像素分割；图卷积网络；互增强；全局空间相关；遥感；IEEE TGRS

Key points:
- Treats superpixel segmentation and pixel classification as mutually enhancing tasks rather than a fixed preprocessing pipeline.
- Published in IEEE TGRS, volume 63 (2025).

Abstract: Most existing hyperspectral image (HSI) classification methods primarily focus on capturing subtle spectral variations by leveraging local spectral-spatial cues derived from patch-level representations. However, limited attention has been given to exploring the global spatial contextual correlations among pixels of HSI. In this study, we propose the Superpixel Segmentation and Classification Mutual Enhancement Network (S2CMEN), a novel framework that integrates global spatial correlations with spectral information through the mutual enhancement of superpixel segmentation and classification. Specifically, a global spatial adaptive module (GSAM) is designed to obtain the direct correlation of the global classes in HSI. It consists of an Adaptive Spectral-Superpixel Network (ASSN) and a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), forming a synergistic architecture that effectively captures global spatial relationships by adaptively deriving superpixel results from HSIs. Notably, GSAM offers a transferable global spatial representation for HSI tasks, enabling integration with other spectral feature extraction models. Furthermore, we develop a Spatial-Spectral Fusion Module (SSFM) to obtain comprehensive spectral features and fuse them with the extracted global spatial features. Finally, under the constraint of a unit loss, the Mutual Enhancement Strategy (MES) can make the superpixel segmentation loss and the classification loss mutually enhance each other for better performance. We conducted extensive experiments on three public datasets. The proposed S2CMEN achieves overall classification accuracies of 97.38%, 92.33%, and 91.38% on Indian Pines, Pavia University, and Houston, respectively, consistently surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods.

## Enhancing urban flow prediction via mutual reinforcement with multi-scale regional information

Authors: Xu Zhang, Mengxin Cao, Yongshun Gong, Xiaoming Wu, Xiangjun Dong, Ying Guo, Long Zhao, Chengqi Zhang
Venue: Neural Networks, vol. 182, 106900 (2025)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2024.106900
Code: https://github.com/CodeZx6/MR-UPF
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mr-ufp.html
Keywords: urban flow prediction, spatial-temporal heterogeneity, contrastive pre-training, random masking, multi-scale region classification, multi-task learning, intelligent transportation systems
Also described as: MR-UFP; mutual reinforcement urban flow prediction; multi-scale regional information; spatial-temporal random masking pre-training; spatial-temporal contrastive pre-training; region classification auxiliary task for traffic prediction; adaptive environment fusion module; urban flow prediction with small or noisy data; spatial-temporal heterogeneity; crowd flow prediction

TL;DR: MR-UFP improves urban flow prediction on small or noisy data by pre-training with spatial-temporal masking and contrastive learning, then jointly training the predictor with a multi-scale region-classification task that mutually reinforces spatial features.

Task: Urban flow prediction (inflow/outflow of city regions)
Pre-training: Spatial-temporal random masking + spatial-temporal contrastive learning
Auxiliary task: Multi-scale region classification that mutually reinforces spatial feature extraction
Other modules: Adaptive environment fusion, real-time graph processing, joint loss for feedback correction
Evaluation: Two real-world datasets; robust with minimal data

Q: Why does MR-UFP work with small or noisy datasets?
A: Spatial feature sensitivity is the bottleneck on small data. MR-UFP pre-trains with masking and contrastive learning to mine heterogeneity directly from historical flows, and turns spatial feature extraction into a mutual-reinforcement task with a multi-scale region-classification auxiliary task.

Q: How are the two tasks balanced?
A: A joint loss function optimises feature embedding and feedback correction between flow prediction and region classification.

Q: How does it relate to MCSTL and ST-CSL?
A: It continues the same line of masked and contrastive pre-training for urban flows introduced in MCSTL (CIKM 2023) and ST-CSL (Knowledge-Based Systems 2023), adding multi-scale regional information and mutual reinforcement.

中文标题: 基于多尺度区域信息互增强的城市流量预测（MR-UFP）
中文摘要: 城市流量预测是智能交通系统的关键。现有方法很少处理城市流量的时空异质性，且通常只从流量本身提取空间特征，在小数据或噪声数据上空间特征敏感性成为瓶颈。MR-UFP 首先用时空随机掩码与时空对比学习预训练，直接从历史流量中挖掘时空异质性；其次通过多尺度区域分类辅助任务，把空间特征提取与嵌入转化为互增强任务，自适应环境融合模块与实时图处理动态关联区域与环境特征；最后设计联合损失平衡两个任务。在两个真实数据集上优于基线，小数据下依然稳健。
中文关键词: 城市流量预测；时空异质性；掩码预训练；对比学习；多尺度区域分类；多任务学习；智能交通；Neural Networks

Key points:
- Spatial-temporal random masking plus contrastive pre-training mines heterogeneity directly from historical flows.
- Spatial feature extraction is reformulated as a mutual-reinforcement task with a multi-scale regional classification auxiliary task, with adaptive environment fusion and real-time graph processing.
- A joint loss balances the two tasks; experiments on two real-world datasets show gains over baselines even with minimal data.

Abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) are essential for modern urban development, with urban flow prediction being a key component. Accurate flow prediction optimizes routes and resource allocation, benefiting residents, businesses, and the environment. However, few methods address the spatial-temporal heterogeneity of urban flows. Existing methods typically capture spatial features solely from urban flows, but spatial feature sensitivity becomes a bottleneck when dealing with small or noisy datasets. To address this issue, we propose a method for urban flow prediction via mutual reinforcement with multi-scale regional information (MR-UFP). Firstly, we employ spatial-temporal random masking and spatial-temporal contrastive learning pre-training to directly mine spatial-temporal heterogeneity from historical flow data. Secondly, we transform the task of spatial feature extraction and embedding for urban flow prediction into a mutual reinforcement task by multi-scale region classification auxiliary task. The adaptive environment fusion module and real-time graph processing dynamically correlate regional and environmental features during flow prediction. To balance the mutual reinforcement of the two tasks, we design a joint loss function to optimize feature embedding and feedback correction, ensuring robust and accurate urban flow prediction. Extensive experiments on two real-world datasets demonstrate that MR-UFP outperforms baseline models, showcasing its robustness and effectiveness even with minimal data.

## Enhancing origin–destination flow prediction via bi-directional spatio-temporal inference and interconnected feature evolution

Authors: Piao Yu, Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Jian Zhang, Haoliang Sun, Junjie Zhang, Xinxin Zhang, Yilong Yin
Venue: Expert Systems with Applications, vol. 264, 125679 (2025)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eswa.2024.125679
Code: https://github.com/CodeZx6/BiST-IF
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/bist-if.html
Keywords: origin-destination flow prediction, OD delay correction, bi-directional attention, mutual information, Out-OD flow, HZMetro, NYC taxi, intelligent transportation
Also described as: BiST-IF; OD flow prediction with delay correction; Out-OD flow; arrival OD flow; OD delay correction ODDC; OD bi-directional attention ODBA; mutual information flow evolution MFE; metro passenger OD flow prediction; inter-station passenger flow prediction; HZMetro Hangzhou metro; NYC-TOD2018 Manhattan taxi zones

TL;DR: BiST-IF predicts metro and taxi origin-destination flows by correcting delayed OD matrices, applying bi-directional origin/destination attention, and letting OD and arrival (Out-OD) flows evolve jointly through mutual-information attention.

Task: Origin-destination (OD) flow prediction between stations or zones
Problem addressed: Delayed availability of OD flows and the unused supplementary signal of arrival (Out-OD) flows
Modules: OD Delay Correction; OD Bi-directional Attention (BiLSTM + origin-wise and destination-wise attention); Mutual Information Flow Evolution (multi-head attention + gated update)
Datasets: HZMetro (80 stations, 10-minute intervals, Jan 2019), NYC-TOD2018 (69 Manhattan taxi zones, 30-minute intervals, Feb–Apr 2018)

Q: What is the OD delay problem?
A: A trip's destination is only known when it ends, so recent OD matrices are incomplete. BiST-IF corrects them using period-delay probability and real-time flow features.

Q: What is Out-OD flow and why use it?
A: Out-OD is the arrival-side OD flow. BiST-IF models the mutual information between OD and Out-OD flows so the two evolve jointly, improving destination-aware inference.

Q: Which datasets were used?
A: HZMetro (Hangzhou metro, 80 stations, 10-minute intervals) and NYC-TOD2018 (69 Manhattan taxi zones, 30-minute intervals).

中文标题: 通过双向时空推理与互联特征演化增强起讫点（OD）流量预测（BiST-IF）
中文摘要: OD 流量预测对智能交通系统中的站间客流预测至关重要。以往方法忽略了 OD 流的延迟，也未利用到达 OD 流（Out-OD）对 OD 流的补充作用。BiST-IF 首先基于周期延迟概率与实时流量特征对 OD 流信息进行校正；其次针对不同周期的流量信息设计双向注意力模块，分解分析 OD 流的时间与流量特征并融合时空特征得到初步预测；随后设计 Out-OD 与 OD 流的互信息模块，建模二者互联的特征演化。在 HZMetro 与 NYC-TOD2018 上评测。
中文关键词: OD 流量预测；起讫点矩阵；OD 延迟校正；双向注意力；互信息；地铁客流；出租车 OD；智能交通

Key points:
- OD Delay Correction estimates delayed OD distributions from periodic patterns and recent Out-OD flows.
- OD Bi-directional Attention extracts trends with BiLSTM and origin-wise plus destination-wise attention.
- Mutual Information Flow Evolution fuses OD and Out-OD features with multi-head attention and gated updates.
- Evaluated on HZMetro (80 stations, 10-minute intervals) and NYC-TOD2018 (69 Manhattan taxi zones, 30-minute intervals).

Abstract: Origin–destination (OD) flow prediction is crucial for predicting inter-station passenger flows in intelligent transport systems. However, previous OD prediction methods have ignored the delay of OD flows and failed to focus on the supplementary effect of the arrival OD flow (Out-OD) flow data on OD flows. We innovatively propose an OD flow prediction method based on Bidirectional Attention and Interconnected Feature Evolution (BiST-IF) to address these challenges. Firstly, we propose a correction method based on period delay probability and real-time flow features for OD flow information. Furthermore, for the flow information of different periods, we design a bi-directional attention module to achieve the preliminary prediction by deconstructing and analyzing the temporal and flow features of OD flow and fusing the temporal and spatial features. After that, we design the mutual information module of Out-OD and OD flows to model their interconnected feature evolution.

## Automatic visual recognition for leaf disease based on enhanced attention mechanism

Authors: Yumeng Yao, Xiaodun Deng, Xu Zhang, Junming Li, Wenxuan Sun, Gechao Zhang
Venue: PeerJ Computer Science, vol. 10, e2365 (2024)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj-cs.2365
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/leaf-disease-attention.html
Keywords: plant leaf disease recognition, tomato disease, attention mechanism, computer vision, smart agriculture
Also described as: tomato leaf disease recognition; plant leaf disease detection; multi-head attention for small lesion detection; Focaler-SIoU loss; leaf disease detection in complex backgrounds; robust to illumination changes; average detection accuracy improved by 10.3%; smart agriculture computer vision; open access PeerJ Computer Science

TL;DR: An enhanced-attention vision model for fast and accurate recognition of tomato leaf diseases, aimed at early disease prevention in agriculture.

Task: Visual recognition (detection) of tomato leaf diseases
Mechanism: Enhanced multi-head attention for small lesion targets; Focaler-SIoU to improve learning on hard samples
Result: Average detection accuracy +10.3% over the baseline model with balanced speed
Open access: Yes, CC BY; also in PubMed Central (PMC11623051)

Q: What makes leaf disease recognition hard?
A: Complex backgrounds and environmental factors such as varying illumination cause confusion between lesions and background, and small lesions carry little information.

Q: What does the method change?
A: It integrates multi-head attention to focus on small tomato lesion targets and adds Focaler-SIoU to strengthen learning on challenging samples, giving a 10.3% improvement in average detection accuracy over the baseline.

中文标题: 基于增强注意力机制的叶片病害自动视觉识别
中文摘要: 叶片病害的高效视觉识别对减少农业经济损失至关重要，但复杂背景与环境因素常导致病斑与背景混淆、小病斑信息难以提取。本文提出基于增强注意力机制的叶片病害视觉识别方法：融合多头注意力以准确识别番茄小病斑目标，在光照变化等复杂条件下保持鲁棒；引入 Focaler-SIoU 增强对困难样本的学习能力。实验表明平均检测精度较基线提升 10.3%，同时保持均衡的识别速度。
中文关键词: 叶片病害识别；番茄病害检测；注意力机制；小目标检测；Focaler-SIoU；智慧农业；开放获取

Key points:
- Open access (CC BY) in PeerJ Computer Science, also indexed in PubMed Central.

Abstract: Recognition methods have made significant strides across various domains, such as image classification, automatic segmentation, and autonomous driving. Efficient identification of leaf diseases through visual recognition is critical for mitigating economic losses. However, recognizing leaf diseases is challenging due to complex backgrounds and environmental factors. These challenges often result in confusion between lesions and backgrounds, limiting information extraction from small lesion targets. To tackle these challenges, this article proposes a visual leaf disease identification method based on an enhanced attention mechanism. By integrating multi-head attention mechanisms, this method accurately identifies small targets of tomato lesions and demonstrates robustness in complex conditions, such as varying illumination. Additionally, the method incorporates Focaler-SIoU to enhance learning capabilities for challenging classification samples. Experimental results showcase that the proposed algorithm enhances average detection accuracy by 10.3% compared to the baseline model, while maintaining a balanced identification speed. This method facilitates rapid and precise identification of tomato diseases, offering a valuable tool for disease prevention and economic loss reduction.

## Spatial-Spectral–Semantic Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning for Hyperspectral Image Classification

Authors: Mengxin Cao, Xu Zhang, Jinyong Cheng, Guixin Zhao, Wei Li, Xiangjun Dong
Venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 62, 1–15 (2024)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1109/TGRS.2024.3434484
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/spatial-spectral-semantic-fsl.html
Keywords: hyperspectral image classification, few-shot learning, cross-domain, spatial-spectral, semantic, remote sensing
Also described as: S3CFSL; spatial-spectral-semantic cross-domain few-shot learning; cross-domain few-shot hyperspectral classification; SSDC spatial and spectral dual channels; CSST cross-spatial-spectral transformer; SEDA semantic-enhanced domain alignment; feature denoising for few-shot HSI; meta-learning source domain target domain hyperspectral; sample selection bias few-shot; water-absorption bands noise HSI

TL;DR: A cross-domain few-shot learner for hyperspectral images that jointly exploits spatial, spectral, and semantic information to classify new scenes from very few labelled samples.

Task: Cross-domain few-shot hyperspectral image classification
Problems addressed: Residual noise after preprocessing; sample-selection bias causing spurious cross-domain correlations
Modules: Spatial and spectral dual channels (SSDC) + cross-spatial-spectral transformer (CSST) as extractor; feature denoising; semantic-enhanced domain alignment (SEDA)
Evaluation: Three public HSI datasets

Q: What is cross-domain few-shot HSI classification?
A: Learning to classify a new hyperspectral scene (target domain) from very few labelled samples by meta-learning on a different, labelled source domain.

Q: How does S3CFSL improve transfer?
A: Feature-denoising operations restore essential information for transferable features, and a semantic-aware domain alignment (SEDA) strengthens the link between cross-domain data and semantic information, improving distributional consistency.

中文标题: 面向高光谱图像分类的空间-光谱-语义跨域小样本学习（S3CFSL）
中文摘要: 高光谱图像预处理通常无法完全消除噪声，在跨域小样本分类等对数据质量要求极高的场景中，残余背景噪声显著影响结果；小样本任务中的样本选择偏差还会导致跨域数据间的虚假统计相关，降低泛化能力。S3CFSL 在特征提取中引入特征去噪以恢复关键信息、促进可迁移信息学习，并通过语义感知策略增强跨域数据与语义信息的关联。具体地，空间与光谱双通道 SSDC 与跨空间-光谱 Transformer CSST 构成特征提取器，特征去噪促进源域与目标域上的元学习，语义增强域对齐 SEDA 提升跨域分布一致性。在三个公开高光谱数据集上优于现有方法。
中文关键词: 高光谱图像分类；跨域小样本学习；特征去噪；语义域对齐；元学习；Transformer；遥感；IEEE TGRS

Key points:
- Published in IEEE TGRS, volume 62 (2024), pages 1-15.

Abstract: Preprocessing procedures are commonly employed to reduce water-absorption bands and noise in hyperspectral images (HSIs). Nevertheless, they typically do not entirely eradicate noise. This is especially evident in scenarios that necessitate data of exceptional quality, such as cross-domain few-shot classification tasks. Within these specific conditions, the influence of remaining background noise on the ultimate results of classification is substantial. Furthermore, the presence of sample selection biases in the few-shot task might lead to the emergence of false statistical correlations between data from distinct domains, resulting in a decrease in the model’s ability to generalize. We propose a new method called spatial-spectral–semantic cross-domain few-shot learning (S3CFSL) to address the challenge. This method promotes the learning of transferable information by incorporating feature denoising operations in the feature extraction process to restore essential information. Concurrently, it enhances cross-domain distributional consistency by introducing a semantic-aware strategy to strengthen the association between cross-domain data and semantic information. Specifically, the spatial and spectral dual channels (SSDCs), in conjunction with the cross-spatial-spectral transformer (CSST), are designed as a feature extractor to acquire interactive spatial-spectral features. The feature-denoising operations can further acquiring transferable information from cross-domain features, thus facilitating meta-learning in both the source domain (SD) and the target domain (TD). Meanwhile, a semantic-enhanced domain alignment (SEDA) is designed to promote domain adaptation by using a semantic-aware strategy, which significantly enhances distributional consistency for cross-domain tasks. Our results exhibit exceptional classification efficacy in comparison to other state-of-the-art approaches on three public HSI datasets.

## Spatio-temporal fusion and contrastive learning for urban flow prediction

Authors: Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Chengqi Zhang, Xiaoming Wu, Ying Guo, Wenpeng Lu, Long Zhao, Xiangjun Dong
Venue: Knowledge-Based Systems, vol. 282, 111104 (2023)
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.knosys.2023.111104
Code: https://github.com/CodeZx6/ST-CSL
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/st-csl.html
Keywords: urban flow prediction, contrastive learning, spatio-temporal fusion, periodicity, functional regions, traffic prediction
Also described as: ST-CSL; spatio-temporal fusion and contrastive learning; temporal-view contrastive learning; spatial-view contrastive learning; urban flow periodicity; similar functional regions; closeness period trend encoders; multi-view urban flow prediction; crowd flow forecasting contrastive

TL;DR: ST-CSL fuses temporal-view and spatial-view contrastive learning so an urban flow predictor captures global periodicity and the hidden flow relationships between functionally similar regions.

Task: Urban flow prediction
Idea: Contrastive learning in the temporal dimension (global periodicity) and the spatial dimension (implied relations between similar regions)
Architecture: Separate closeness, period, and trend encoders fused by a residual network
Code: https://github.com/CodeZx6/ST-CSL

Q: What limitation of earlier methods does ST-CSL target?
A: They are insensitive to periodic changes in urban flows and rarely consider the implied spatial and temporal correlations between similar functional areas.

Q: What do the two contrastive views provide?
A: The temporal view captures the distribution and change of global urban-flow periodicity; the spatial view captures the implied flow variation between similar regions.

中文标题: 时空融合与对比学习的城市流量预测（ST-CSL）
中文摘要: 城市流量预测对城市规划、管理与安全至关重要，但流量固有的不稳定性要求融合多视角影响因素。现有方法对周期变化不敏感，也很少考虑相似功能区之间隐含的时空关联。ST-CSL 在时间与空间维度上基于对比学习构建视图提取模块：时间视图获得全局流量周期性的分布与变化，空间视图获得相似区域间隐含的流量变化关系，从而捕捉城市流量变化的高层语义特征。
中文关键词: 城市流量预测；对比学习；时空融合；周期性；功能区；Knowledge-Based Systems

Key points:
- Temporal-view extraction captures the distribution and change of global urban-flow periodicity.
- Spatial-view extraction captures implied flow variation between similar regions.
- Separate closeness, period, and trend encoders are fused by a residual fusion network.

Abstract: Urban flow prediction is critical for urban planning, management, and safety. However, owing to the inherent instability of urban flows, prediction accuracy requires the fusion of multi-view influencing factors. Current prediction methods are insensitive to periodic changes in urban flows, and rarely consider the implied spatial and temporal correlations between similar functional areas. Thus, we propose a method based on spatiotemporal fusion and contrastive learning. We construct an extraction module of spatial and temporal views based on contrastive learning in the spatial and temporal dimensions. With the temporal view extraction, we can obtain the distribution and change in the global urban flow periodicity. Using the spatial view extraction, we can obtain the implied flow variation relationship between similar regions.

## Mask- and Contrast-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Learning for Urban Flow Prediction

Authors: Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Xinxin Zhang, Xiaoming Wu, Chengqi Zhang, Xiangjun Dong
Venue: CIKM 2023, pp. 3298–3307
DOI: https://doi.org/10.1145/3583780.3614958
Code: https://github.com/CodeZx6/MCSTL
Page: https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mcstl.html
Keywords: urban flow prediction, masked pre-training, contrastive learning, graph attention, spatio-temporal learning, CIKM
Also described as: MCSTL; mask- and contrast-enhanced spatio-temporal learning; masked pre-training for urban flow; contrastive pre-training for traffic flow; global-local cross-attention; inter-regional attention weights; spatio-temporal heterogeneity urban flow prediction; UFP urban flow prediction; CIKM 2023 urban flow paper

TL;DR: MCSTL pre-trains an urban flow model with a mask-reconstruction task across space and time and a graph-based contrastive task that weights regions by inter-regional attention, then fine-tunes for flow prediction.

Task: Urban flow prediction (UFP)
Pre-training tasks: Mask-enhanced reconstruction across space and time; contrastive learning with global-local cross-attention
Graph component: Inter-regional attention weights determine region significance
Evaluation: Real-world urban flow datasets vs. state-of-the-art models
Open access: Yes, ACM Digital Library

Q: What does MCSTL model that earlier methods did not?
A: Heterogeneity in both space and time at once: regional correlations vary across timestamps, so MCSTL learns time-varying spatio-temporal representations.

Q: How is MCSTL trained?
A: Two pre-training tasks, mask-enhanced reconstruction and contrastive learning with global-local cross-attention, produce two encoders that are then used for flow forecasting.

中文标题: 掩码与对比增强的时空学习用于城市流量预测（MCSTL）
中文摘要: 城市流量预测是智能交通系统的关键任务，但既有研究很少同时考察空间与时间两方面的异质性，即区域相关性会随时间变化。本文提出带掩码与对比增强的时空学习框架：设计掩码增强的预训练任务学习跨空间与时间维度的潜在相关性，并用基于图的方法通过区域间注意力权重提取区域重要性；进一步设计带全局-局部交叉注意力的对比预训练任务获取区域的对比相关性。两个训练好的编码器可捕获随时间变化的潜在时空表示。在真实城市流量数据集上优于现有方法。
中文关键词: 城市流量预测；掩码预训练；对比学习；图注意力；时空异质性；CIKM 2023；开放获取

Key points:
- A mask-enhanced pre-training task learns latent correlations across spatial and temporal dimensions.
- A graph-based method uses inter-regional attention weights to derive contrastive correlations between regions.
- Published open access in the ACM Digital Library (CIKM 2023, pages 3298-3307).

Abstract: As a critical mission of intelligent transportation systems, urban flow prediction (UFP) benefits in many city services including trip planning, congestion control, and public safety. Despite the achievements of previous studies, limited efforts have been observed on simultaneous investigation of the heterogeneity in both space and time aspects. That is, regional correlations would be variable at different timestamps. In this paper, we propose a spatio-temporal learning framework with mask and contrast enhancements to capture spatio-temporal variabilities among city regions. We devise a mask-enhanced pre-training task to learn latent correlations across the spatial and temporal dimensions, and then a graph-based method is developed to extract the significance of regions by using the inter-regional attention weights. To further acquire contrastive correlations of regions, we elaborate a pre-trained contrastive learning task with the global-local cross-attention mechanism. Thereafter, two well-trained encoders have strong capability to capture latent spatio-temporal representations for the flow forecasting with time-varying. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world urban flow datasets demonstrate that our method compares favorably with other state-of-the-art models.

}
